description: Run-stage scripts invoking mise-wrapped commands (just qualitygate, sd) fail with 'Config files in /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml are not trusted' whenever the sandbox/home is recycled or .mise.toml changes, killing the whole stage before any code runs (run 01M1XCHJTDBJKZ31VFMY1KD61Q tester stage).
resolution: Immediate: 'mise trust /repos/denkhaus/fabro/.mise.toml' once per environment (done this session). Durable: stage bootstrap or justfile entry should export MISE_YES=1 or pre-trust before invoking mise-dependent recipes.

description: rg -rn is never a valid flag combo: rg parses -r <text> as REPLACE-with-literal. Run 01M22X87J1RKQ6A8FZB7RC2RN8: 'rg -rn "is_engine_stamped_key"' replaced every match with literal 'n', producing 'pub fn n(key: &str...)', which was then misdiagnosed as 'sandbox rg unreliable' (false lore, cost 2 diagnostic rounds). Use -n alone for line numbers.
resolution: Discipline line added to .fabro/workflows/develop/prompts/implementer.md retracting the 'sandbox rg unreliable' lore (seed fabro-2eb6).

description: Semantics change in fabro-tool inherit_parent_target (fabro-b4ed, run 01M2GVW7GGGB19ZZ9NBN2H5FDC) passed the implementer's crate-scoped verify but red-lined the tester: the fabro-server integration fixture lib/apps/fabro-server/src/run_tool_create.rs builds a parent via test_run_spec() whose pull_request settings stay None, so under the new option-(a) semantics the child correctly inherits the base branch and the checkout assertion reads 'original'. Lesson: any change to inherited-target semantics must update downstream fixture parents to enable pull_request settings when the test means to exercise run-branch chaining. Also: after editing a src-integrated test file, confirm nextest actually recompiled — a stale binary reported the pre-edit panic line.
resolution: Fixture parent now sets pull_request enabled before inherit, matching the new chaining precondition; test passes and full fabro-server suite is green (939/939).

content: bun run generate in lib/packages/fabro-api-client works in the agent sandbox if java is provisioned via mise first

gh pitfalls hit live 2026-09-28: merge 504 can be a false negative (recheck state=MERGED before failing); gh pr view by-branch also returns CLOSED PRs (reuse open PRs only via gh pr list --state open); force-with-lease needs fetch --prune after the remote branch was deleted by a merged/closed PR.

content: fabro-api-client regen without a working java: run the SAME pinned generator via Docker (openapitools/openapi-generator-cli:v7.20.0 generate -i <spec> -o /local/lib/packages/fabro-api-client/src with the repo mounted at /local), then bun run scripts/normalize-generated.ts, then fix root-owned output via an alpine chown sidecar (bun re-creates files through directory write access). LOCAL test-stack deploys are ALWAYS just up (cached loop: SPA, binary, image, CLI, compose) — docker compose up --build builds nothing here and cargo build -p <name> drifts with upstream package renames; PRODUCTION is just image-release + fabro-tofu apply, never hand-composed.

description: Changing the embedded FABRO_GIT_SHA length (fabro_build_support::SHORT_SHA_LEN, fabro-6ffb 7->12) silently breaks the fabro-test insta BUILD filter regex (lib/foundation/fabro-test/src/lib.rs INSTA_FILTERS, the ([0-9a-f]{7} date...) pattern) because the filter hardcodes the old length: version snapshots then diff on every commit. Length-bearing snapshot filters must be updated in the same diff as the length constant; symptom is a snapshot diff showing a raw sha where [BUILD] used to be.
resolution: Updated the filter to {12} in the same diff (fabro-6ffb); future length changes must grep INSTA_FILTERS for the old length before landing.

description: Piping  into a python one-liner that crashes still creates the record — the CLI already wrote it (fabro sprint 19: d7e7+3523 silently duplicated f93b+c167 and had to be closed as dupes). Same class as the fabro create ghost-run rule.
resolution: write seeds CLI json to a FILE first, then parse the file; never pipe create-family commands into a consumer that can die; sweep the tracker diff for surprise new ids before committing

description: A tracker close reason containing BACKTICKS was passed through the bash() command line (seeds close <id> --reason "..."): bash executed the backticked fragments as command substitution. 'start -> env_guard -> tracker_guard' ran the command 'start' with stdout REDIRECTED to env_guard and tracker_guard, which CREATED three empty files at the repo root; the recorded close reason lost every backticked phrase. It went unnoticed until but status showed three 'A' entries beside the tracker file.
resolution: For any CLI write whose text may contain backticks, $() or >, write the payload to a file and pass it as --reason "$(cat /tmp/reason.txt)" (command substitution happens once, on that path only). After every shell-based tracker write, run but status / git status and remove stray A entries before committing — a stray file would otherwise ride the next sweep commit.

description: rg -rn does NOT mean recursive+line-numbers in the way expected: -r takes the NEXT TOKEN as its REPLACE value, so -rn silently replaces every match with the literal n in the OUTPUT (observed twice in one session 2026-10-14: EnvironmentErrorKind::n in results, gate-measure scan confusion). Use -n -r separately or omit -r; the corrupted display looks like real source content.
resolution: Never write -rn; use rg -n alone, and -r VALUE as an explicit separate flag.

content: The fabro-test workbench has a SINGLE-PROBE mode: `nu scripts/workbench.nu probe <name>` (plus --expect to override) — it runs one facet without board clean, platform checks, or the mini integration. During incident triage, NEVER re-run the full bench to re-check one facet: identify the suspected rows first (run list via `fabro ps -a --json` + bench label, or the platform checks via `source scripts/workbench.nu; platform-checks`), then re-run exactly those. User directive 2026-10-27 after three full bench runs (~15 min and real model cost each) where a single probe would have answered.

GitHub read-after-write races: any immediate read that follows a create (label-filtered list, PR body fetch, issue read) races the index and must poll (~2s convergence, 6x2s is the proven pattern). Two witnesses now: the P4 work-CLI list row (sprint 53, denkhaus/work#10..#12) and the publish-bridge PR body fetch (bench 1027-162117: PR #87 body was generated prose but the immediate fetch failed the bridge; fixed in fabro-test PR #88 with the same poll).

description: Literal parentheses inside a nu $"..." interpolation are parsed as a subexpression and executed as a command — scripts/verify.nu:292 prints a status line containing '(full crate suite: ...)' inside $"" and crashes with 'Command full not found' exactly when the full-crate-suite test arm fires (any implementer diff that edits existing tests in a touched crate).
resolution: Workaround in run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW: run the intended nextest slice directly (cargo nextest run -p <crate> --no-fail-fast). Durable fix is a loop-asset item: strip the literal parens or build the label by concatenation.

name: gate-red triage: parent-commit worktree repro with shared target dir
description: When a tester gate-red bounces the implementer, classify item-caused vs pre-existing environmental by reproducing ONE representative failing test on the untouched parent commit in a throwaway worktree sharing the main target dir: git worktree add /tmp/qg-parent <parent-sha> && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<repo>/target cargo nextest run -p <crate> <test>. Build cost ~2-5 min once; a reproduce-on-parent FAIL proves the break is environmental/pre-existing (this run: docker daemon absent + engine-injected FABRO_SERVER default breaking parse_settings_command and all docker-acquiring CLI it-tests, fabro run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW), which routes Blocked instead of chasing phantom regressions in the item diff.

Literal parentheses inside a nu $"..." interpolation are parsed as a subexpression and executed as a command — scripts/verify.nu:292 prints a status line containing '(full crate suite: ...)' inside $" interpolation, so every verify run that reaches the full-crate-suite arm dies with 'Command full not found' before running nextest. RECURRED run 01M621RW4YPD19X5E2VMC054YW (implementer visit 2, again blocking the fabro-cli full-suite arm). Still unfixed in scripts/verify.nu.
resolution: Open loop-asset bug (scripts/verify.nu is fs_hide-bound for the implementer; report-don't-fix). Interim workaround: when the verify run dies at line 292, run the intended 'cargo nextest run -p <crate> --no-fail-fast' directly. Durable fix belongs to a loop-asset item: strip the parens or build the label by string concatenation.

content: just vendor <cmd> --message breaks on any multi-word message: the recipe passes *args into `nu scripts/vendor-sync.nu {{ args }}` UNQUOTED - bash chokes on parens, nu sees extra positionals. Call `nu scripts/vendor-sync.nu export petri --message "..."` directly (same ceremony, quoting survives, multiline bodies work). AGENTS.md documents the just form only.
The repo grep TOOL silently finds nothing under vendor/petri (ignore-file handling); ripgrep via shell with --no-ignore sees the tree. Any vendor-tree search: rg --no-ignore.

description: Root-owned /tmp/fx made all 129 CLI ITs fail instantly; root cause is external Docker test runs creating root-owned fixture dirs.
resolution: Docker-mounted rm as user-space sudo substitute; suite green after (1094/1094).

description: RC-behind-pipe recidivism: twice in ONE session (2026-11-01) an exit code was read behind a pipe (docker exec | head; git diff | rg | head) despite the documented rule and its live incidents. Both would have been silent false-green proofs without manual repetition.
resolution: Convention: read a gated exit code as its OWN line — the command, then rc=$? immediately after, never a pipeline member. If the output needs trimming, capture to a file first and grep the file.

content: grill premise check for CLI surface names: verify the args tree BEFORE pitching a facade-family name — fabro RunCommands FLATTENS to top level (`fabro create`/`fabro attach` are top-level commands, NOT `fabro run <sub>`), so the grilled `fabro run mark` presumed a structure that did not exist and needed a same-session user correction round (run+optional-subcommand + runtime workflow guard). One `rg -n enum.*Commands + #[command(flatten)]` in args.rs before the pitch would have caught it (sprint 73).

TERMINOLOGY (user directive 2026-11-02, sprint 74): a work item is ALWAYS "work-item" in prose and work_item in identifiers — never a bare "item". Bare "item" does not say what kind of item it names. Applies to chat, docs, code, API fields, prompts, commit messages.

title: Door symmetry: agent tools and CLI facades in lockstep
rationale: Command stages (scripts) and agent stages (tools) both work the orchestration surfaces; a surface that exists on only one side forces workarounds (shell escape hatches, context pipes as the only road). The sprint-73 doors landed CLI-first; the user directed lockstep sync as standing policy.

description: Sprint-75 note unrecoverable from its ledger pointer; reconstruction cost one orient phase
resolution: Note reconstructed 2026-11-04 from commit messages + epic #1107 body; standing rule: notes live in the ledger, full text

content: Chat replies are German but the DOMAIN VOCABULARY stays English (user correction 2026-11-07): Gear, Lap, Adjudicator, Merger, Watchdog, Window, Fork — never translated ("Getriebe"/"Lappen" are not words of this domain). The GLOSSARY is the binding vocabulary for chat too; German grammar around English terms is fine, invented translations are not.

Skill texts are INSTRUCTIONS, not incident chronicles (user directive): no years, no old-error references, no "this session got it wrong" narratives inside skill files. State the rule and how to follow it; the evidence story lives in incidents.md, mulch, or the tracker. Applies to every skill edit in every repo of the line.

Lane admission is decided PER ITEM, never per bundle (user directive 2026-11-07): a tranche proposal presents every candidate separately with its named vet result; the user decides item by item. Same-session items get heightened scrutiny — an unreviewed body or a just-corrected hypothesis is not yet a vetted demand. The sprint-81 evening session bundled three items into one recommended-set option and had it ratified in one click.

Bench output capture and crash recovery: a full workbench run ALWAYS writes its complete output to a file (never tail-capture a background bench — a lost facet table tempts a full rerun). When a run crashes AFTER the probes completed, the recovery is the crashed leg plus single-probe drives of the suspects — the completed probe pass stands as evidence; a full rerun for a lost table is pure waste (user correction after a 15-min redundant round).

Never block the session on a scheduled-platform wait: a cron tick minutes away gets a BACKGROUND watcher (notify on completion) while the session keeps working; a foreground sleep-loop that long is dead time the user pays for (user correction 2026-11-07: a 15-min wait on the next gear tick blocked the whole session).

description: Line down 4h20m (03:50-08:15 UTC): every API/DB op 500, UI empty, automations dead — root cause was a full host disk from never-pruned run sandboxes, misread initially as a server/DB problem.
resolution: Label-filtered docker prunes on the host freed 364.7 GB (containers 303.4 + anonymous volumes 61.35); server self-recovered without restart; retention gap filed as denkhaus/work#1185 (needs-user).

content: UI work batches into ONE release, never one-feature cycles: with the fabro turnaround costs (release build + link + image + compose, ~15-30 min each), landing features individually and rebuilding per feature wastes hours and ships incomplete releases the operator then tests piecemeal (2026-11-08: observations columns landed alone, the tiles/verdict/work-view stayed design-only in the same "new version" — operator rightfully flagged the uncoordinated cycle). The batch rule: compose the UI batch first (all visible surfaces), implement in one phase, ONE verification round, ONE PR/merge, ONE image build; the operator reloads once and sees everything. Same amortization logic as sprint batching, applied to release contents.

description: Two background transfers died mid-session by their own pkill; the rsync had to be restarted, losing transfer minutes on a 2.2 Mbit line.
resolution: Kill by exact name or PID; a survivor pattern is nohup + disown for transfers meant to outlive the session.

name: image-push-via-host-egress
description: Image pushes from the home line: ~2.2 Mbit uplink makes every multi-GB GHCR blob upload die at the ack timeout (buildkit AND docker daemon both; per-connection throttling made single connections crawl at KB/s). The working pattern (2026-11-08): transfer the docker-save tar to the production host (netcup-5) over rsync -P (resumable, ~250 KB/s, hours), then crane push FROM the host (datacenter uplink, seconds; crane 0.22.1 installed at /usr/local/bin/crane there, GHCR auth via /root/.docker/config.json). Beware: crane v0.8.0 corrupts docker-archive pushes (invalid tar header on pull) — use v0.22.1+, and verify with a host-side docker pull before the tofu apply.

content: The .todo/ directory at the repo root is a TRANSIENT workaround (user convention 2026-11-08, extended 2026-11-09): todo.md holds tasks below the work-item threshold, HANDOFF-DEPLOY-WINDOW.md carries the dark-window plan — for daily work there are NO md handoffs, only the tracker and mulch (user directive 2026-11-09). The files exist only while they have open entries and DISAPPEAR after the work is done: the consuming session deletes them, and the directory once empty. They never become permanent artifacts, never carry history (that is the tracker and the ledger), and sessions may update them with current states but must not archive them. The ledger note of the session that empties the directory records the closure.

root .dockerignore is shared by EVERY root-context build: the release pipeline stages tmp/docker-context (must stay allowed), the local just-up image build COPYs from it, and any relaxation for one consumer breaks another — touch it only with all three consumers named (2026-11-10: the engine-cook relaxation broke just up within the hour)

opaque/composite keys (owner/repo#N) never ride a PATH parameter — the encoded slash 400s bare; query parameters carry them (2026-11-10: the work-item door, found only by the live proof — mocks and conformance were blind)

the local stack environment catalog is BENCH CONFIGURATION: live-testing against it (e.g. nulling the toolchain image to drive a { path } compile) must be RESTORED before any bench round — an unrestored flip made 18 probes red at once (2026-11-10, the tail window)

name: fabro events read verb
description: Diagnosis entry point: `fabro events <run> --pretty [--tail N] [--since 42m] [--follow] [--json]` already renders a run stream, including visit.completed failures and the run.lifecycle reason with the full enriched error tail. Sprint 84 retro filed work#1274 for this verb believing it did not exist — the session had used raw curl for run event access. Before filing a CLI-verb demand, grep lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/args.rs for the wanted surface (commit 1bfe62577 predates the fork).

content: just vendor export <name> -m "<message>" mangles spaced messages: the justfile forwards *args space-joined into bash, multi-word flags split, and nu rejects the extra positionals. For long messages call the script directly from the repo root: nu scripts/vendor-sync.nu export -m "<message>" <name> (same cwd assumptions, same flags).

description: A copied check with the wrong failure signal is worse than no check: it looks like protection while gating nothing.
resolution: Port the detection mechanic (nu-check / diagnostics parsing), prove the copy with a deliberate red arm before trusting it.

content: release version bump recipe: bumping the workspace version REQUIRES regenerating Cargo.lock in the SAME commit (cargo metadata writes it) — the lock carries every internal crate version string, and --locked fails for any fresh resolve (the host-release fresh clone hits it first). fork.40 window 2026-11-17: the bump missed it and the first host build died at lock resolution.

fabro CLI is mise-managed globally (2026-11-19): ~/.config/mise/config.toml pins github:denkhaus/fabro to the fork.N tag; the github backend resolves the release asset per platform (SLSA provenance verified) — hand-built http: URLs 404 because release asset names carry the SHORT version (fabro-0.362.0-fork.N-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz), not the sha-suffixed tag. Upgrade = bump the version in global config. Releases still lack the .sha256 asset the fabro upgrade door expects (host-release.nu computes and only prints the digest); ~/.fabro/bin/fabro stays as shadowed fallback.

name: edit-file-backtick-old-string
description: The edit_file tool silently fails to match an old_string that contains backticks (the output-hygiene backtick handling appears to reach edit parameters): every multi-line old_string containing a backtick returned 'not found' while backtick-free strings of the same shape matched, and write_file accepts backticks fine. Workaround: anchor edits on backtick-free lines, or rewrite the whole file with write_file. Observed on fabro-web ask-fabro-sidebar.tsx during work#1452 (run 01M7SQC6YA6YJTGKBV037DW386).

content: Timezone trap (2026-11-19): fabro events prints Berlin wall-clock with a Z suffix (11:07 = 11:07 Berlin), while gh JSON fields (mergedAt) are true UTC — never diff them directly; convert before correlating run windows with release timestamps.

Develop worklist order (2026-11-19): the line claims by the tracker worklist order, not by the session sprint composition — sprint 92 anchored #1463/#1448 and the lap claimed #1452. Sprint anchors for line work are expectations, never promises; compose from the worklist head or accept what the line picks.

name: journal-census-duplication
description: Arch-review candidate (2026-11-19, Worth exploring): the run-census is duplicated — friction-score.nu counts develop-runs-in-window by substring-scanning journals while loop-digest.nu classifies journals from a workflow-signature map that still names two RETIRED workflows (select→revisor, analyze→architect), and friction-score headers a dead consumer (the architect workflow). "Develop runs completed in window" is one `fabro ps -a --workflow develop --json` read (server truth); delete the journal-scan arm, retire or reduce loop-digest. Script-layer consolidation, no promotion.

name: checkpoint-commit-door
description: Arch-review candidate (2026-11-19, Worth exploring; ADR-0029 tension flagged): the gates reconstruct which commits belong to a run by grepping git log for the subject mark `fabro(<id>):` and the trailer `Fabro-Run: <id>` — strings whose authority lives in petri checkpoint.rs (RUN_TRAILER); a format tweak is a silent vacuous match (one incident on record: a regex-shaped mark silently matched nothing). Deepening: expose the run checkpoint/journal commit shas through the timeline door (operations/timeline.rs; run channel reaches sandbox gates via FABRO_SERVER) so run-base is a thin call over engine-owned data. The anti-shortlist keeps gate POLICY in scripts — this promotes the base DATA only.
Session-side branch work leaves no claim surface: the claim ledger only records RUN claims, claim_next neither reads item bodies nor respects an explicit do-not-re-implement state section.
resolution: Before local session work on a lane-assigned item, release or move the lane assignment (fabro work lane) and restore it when handing back. Incident 2026-11-19: work#1416/#1465/#1361 each implemented twice - session PRs #611/#616 predated the line claims by 1h45m/2h50m and were still re-implemented (six duplicate PRs needed case-by-case adjudication); the run-planner body-binding arm stays open.
